source_user: An agent repeatedly calls a calculator when the answer is already known. Design metrics and an intervention. Scenario variant 292: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure unnecessary calls, tool success, final correctness, trajectory length, tool latency, and recovery; add a stop/no-tool evaluation and preference or reward signal.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: the calculator is optional, arithmetic is deterministic, and requests can be replayed with fixed prompts, model/version, tool policy, workload mix, and timeout. Do not infer that a successful tool call was necessary. Hypothesis: on prompts whose arithmetic is directly inferable, a stop/no-tool policy can reduce unnecessary calculator calls and trajectory length by at least 30% without reducing exact final-answer correctness by more than 1 percentage point; test this rather than assuming it.

Measure per request whether a call was counterfactually necessary, tool-call rate and success/error/timeout rate, exact final correctness, calibration or abstention, trajectory turns/tokens, tool latency in ms, end-to-end latency, recovery after failed calls, and cost. Run a randomized held-out A/B test of baseline versus intervention, with no-tool and necessary-call controls, fixed seeds where possible, matched strata, blinded correctness review, and confidence intervals. Keep tool-required cases separate.

Confounders include arithmetic difficulty, hidden tool-required cases, prompt mix, model/runtime changes, caching, concurrency, timeout policy, evaluator bias, and reward leakage. Preference or reward is auxiliary only and must be audited against exact correctness. Use shadow mode then a bounded canary with hard correctness, error, latency, and cost gates; retain a tool-required fallback and roll back on correctness loss beyond the bound or SLO regression. Evidence required: replay logs, independently checked labels, stratified A/B results with intervals, and rollback records.

quality_dimensions.safety_limits: Shadow then bounded canary; hard correctness/SLO gates and fallback.
quality_dimensions.measurement_plan: Per-request counterfactual A/B replay with controls.

risks: Counterfactual labels and aggregate averages can mislead.
Workload, model, topology, or runtime changes can confound results.
Mitigations can trade latency for correctness, cost, memory, or token loss.
evidence_required: Replayable traces, independently verified correctness labels, stratified repeated trials with confidence intervals, and canary/rollback telemetry.

source_user: A sparse MoE service has uneven expert load and tail latency. Analyze likely causes and experiments. Scenario variant 4: include an explicit falsifiable hypothesis and a controlled experiment.
source_assistant: Answer should state assumptions, a falsifiable hypothesis, measurements, expected confounders, and rollback criteria. Minimum technical points: measure routing distribution, expert capacity overflow, all-to-all time, token dropping/padding, placement, batch composition, and compare routing/capacity policies.
corrected_answer:
Assumptions: routing is top-k or equivalent sparse routing, expert capacity and placement are configurable, and tail latency is measured end to end with synchronized clocks. Do not assume skew alone is causal. Hypothesis: hot experts and/or cross-device all-to-all congestion cause queueing and tail latency; reducing skew or improving placement/capacity should lower p95/p99 without unacceptable token loss or quality change. Test with fixed model, hardware/topology, software, request mix, sequence lengths, concurrency, and seeds where supported.

Instrument per batch and expert: routed-token counts, top-k probabilities/entropy, load max/mean and coefficient of variation, capacity factor, overflow and dropped tokens, padding, queue/service and expert-compute time, dispatch/combine time, all-to-all bytes and duration, errors, placement and locality, batch composition, throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency, memory, and output correctness. Run matched randomized replay or factorial comparisons, changing separately routing/capacity policy, placement, and batching; include topology controls and verify outputs against a reference.

Confounders include sequence and batch mix, warm-up, topology/oversubscription, kernels, clock throttling, host scheduling, admission control, and cache effects. Mitigate first with admission/batching and placement, then bounded routing/capacity changes; never silently drop tokens. Use shadow replay, a small canary, hard quality/overflow/drop/p99/memory gates, and automatic fallback to the last known-good configuration. Evidence required: synchronized per-rank traces, topology inventory, repeated matched trials, confidence intervals, and correctness/overflow results.

quality_dimensions.safety_limits: Shadow then bounded canary; hard correctness/SLO gates and fallback.
